commentary_segments.text: Nevertheless better matching can be obtained by means of capacitors rather than with transistors. If a resolution of 10 bit can be easily obtained with a resistor bank, then 12 bit can be obtained with a matched capacitor bank (see Chapter 15). An example of such 3-bit capacitor bank is shown in this slide. The larger capacitor 4C consists of 4 equal capacitors C laid out properly (see Chapter 15). commentary_segments.text_raw:
The output voltage holds the voltage obtained during the previous clock phase.
In clock phase W2, the charge of the capacitors which belong to the switches connected to
ground, is transferred to the output capacitor 8C.
The output voltage then changes depending on the charge transferred from these capacitors.
Note that this circuit suffers from the same problems as switched capacitors filters. They can
easily achieve a 70 dB dynamic range corresponding to about 12 bit, but not much more.

commentary_text:
Nevertheless better matching can be obtained by means of capacitors rather than with transistors. If a resolution of 10 bit can be easily obtained with a resistor bank, then 12 bit can be obtained with a matched capacitor bank (see Chapter 15). An example of such 3-bit capacitor bank is shown in this slide. The larger capacitor 4C consists of 4 equal capacitors C laid out properly (see Chapter 15). By means of charge redistribution, the output voltage is a sum of binary fractions of the reference voltage V . ref In clock phase W1 (as shown) all binary capacitors are charged to V . ref
